chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), from Ali (peace be upon him)
that he used to walk in one shoe and repair the other, and he did not see any problem with that
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to walk in one shoe while repairing the other according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the practical simplicity and frugality of Imam al-Sadiq (AS), illustrating that wearing one sandal while repairing the other is a permissible and unobjectionable practice (la yara bi-dhaka ba'san). It serves as a foundational evidence for the permissibility of asymmetrical footwear in Shia jurisprudence, emphasizing ease in daily life over rigid uniformity. The narration underscores the Imam's approach to removing unnecessary hardship from the community regarding minor aspects of dress and conduct.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, from Ali<sup>asws</sup>,
if one were to walk in one shoe and repair the other, he<sup>asws</sup> did not see any problem with that’.
en.sarwar: 6. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from al-Nawfaliy from al-Sakuniy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that
Ali ibn al-Husayn, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, walked with one shoe while repairing the other one, and he did not consider it harmful.’”
